---

First developed in the Puddles about 20 years ago, this stimulant has grown from a diversion of the wretched poor to a habit for well- heeled merchants and nobles. At low doses, grit provides the physical body with increased energy while stimulating the idle mind into effortless flights of creative fancy. Abuse of the drug leads to severe hallucinations, numbing, and uncontrollable rage. Grit is produced by grinding down alchemically-enhanced barbarian chew, which is mixed with toxic plant- based substances, such as bitterbark or redroot. The powder is very expensive and highly addictive.

The save for addiction to grit is DC 15, and the addiction has the [virulent](/Traits.aspx?ID=162) trait.

 **Saving Throw** DC 15 Fortitude; **Onset** 1 minute; **Maximum Duration** 4 hours; **Stage 1** +1 item bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3), [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4), and [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks (10 minutes); **Stage 2** +1 item bonus to Athletics, Crafting, and Performance checks, –2 item penalty to Perception checks (1 hour); **Stage 3** –4 item penalty to Perception checks (1 hour); **Stage 4** as stage 3 (1 hour); **Stage 5** [confusion](/Conditions.aspx?ID=5) (1 round); **Stage 6** [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=38) (remaining duration)

This [caligni](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=18)-made, murky-green drug supercharges a creature's olfactory senses at the expense of dulling their mind. Popular throughout the Darklands for its ability to transform normally dull scents and flavors into intense, euphoric experiences, grolna can also be a great aid to trackers who want to follow scent trails, turning ordinary humanoids into effective bloodhounds.

 Taking an additional dose of grolna while affected by the effects of stage 1 of a previous dose resets the duration of stage 1 and postpones the onset of stage 2 effects.

 **Saving Throw** DC 13 Fortitude; **Onset** 1 minute; **Maximum Duration** 8 hours; **Stage 1** gain [scent](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=33) (imprecise) 30 feet, gain a +3 item bonus to [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) checks to follow tracks, and become [stupefied 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=37) (1 hour); **Stage 2** stupefied 2 (6 hours)

A _growth gun_ is a _+1 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [hand cannon](/Weapons.aspx?ID=193)_ made from the regenerative flesh of a [hydra](/Monsters.aspx?ID=269), [troll](/Monsters.aspx?ID=395), or other similar creature. It has an attached flesh sac that slowly replenishes one shot each round and can be loaded like a normal round of ammunition. It fires regenerating gobbets of flesh, bone, or teeth, determined by the damage type selected for its [modular](/Traits.aspx?ID=271) trait. A growth gun can be fired underwater, though it's still limited by the selected damage type as normal.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per minute;   **Effect** Make a ranged Strike. On a hit, the creature becomes covered in a mass of flesh that continues to grow on the target for a brief time. The creature becomes [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35) for 1 round, after which the growth withers and falls off.

**Craft Requirements** The initial raw materials must include the flesh of a creature with [regeneration](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=26).

---

A _growth gun_ is a _[+1 striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2861) [hand cannon](/Weapons.aspx?ID=523)_ made from the regenerative flesh of a [hydra](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3064), [troll](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=478), or other similar creature. It has an attached flesh sac that slowly replenishes one shot each round and can be loaded like a normal round of ammunition. It fires regenerating gobbets of flesh, bone, or teeth, determined by the damage type selected for its [modular](/Traits.aspx?ID=807) trait. A _growth gun_ can be fired underwater, though it’s still limited by the selected damage type as normal.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact ([magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [transmutation](/Traits.aspx?ID=157)) **Frequency** once per minute;   **Effect** Make a ranged [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=1167). On a hit, the creature becomes covered in a mass of flesh that continues to grow on the target for a brief time. The creature becomes [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) 1 for 1 round, after which the growth withers and falls off.

**Craft Requirements** The initial raw materials must include the flesh of a creature with [regeneration](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=72).

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Highhelm](/Sources.aspx?ID=204) pg. 87

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn gloves

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Danila Kenn and Depa Stepwell of Common Goods developed these gloves after complaints from an exhausted grindlegrub rancher. Since their development, the gloves have become popular not just among grindlegrub ranchers, but laborers of all kinds in Stonebreach. The thick gloves are designed to help ranchers hold on to the squirming, slimy bodies of grindlegrubs, and help soothe the wear and tear of the day while restoring energy for after-hours pursuits. While wearing the gloves, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) checks. The gripping power of the gloves provides you with a +2 circumstance bonus to Reflex saves to [Grab an Edge](/Actions.aspx?ID=95). If you roll a success to Grab an Edge, you get a critical success instead, as the _gripping gloves_ allow you to hold on even with just a few fingertips.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You rub your hands together and take a deep breath to prepare for the rest of your day. You regain 3d8+10 Hit Points and feel refreshed, losing the [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=15) condition. As normal for effects that remove fatigue, this doesn't remove any underlying source of fatigue, such as lack of sleep, causing the condition to return if the underlying source isn't addressed.

This large drum is made of hardwood and horse hide, with white silhouettes of coursing stallions along its circumference. This drum grants you a +1 item bonus to [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45) checks while playing music with the instrument.

For 10 minutes, mounted allies within a 60-foot emanation gain a +10-foot status bonus to their mount’s Speeds. A _guardian aluum charm_ grants control over powerful [aluums](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=113)—metal and stone constructs created by the Pactmasters to help maintain order in the city of Katapesh. As long as you wear a guardian aluum's linked _guardian aluum charm_, that aluum follows your verbal commands.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command, envision;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The charm grants you control over an aluum you can see within 60 feet, as long as the target aluum is level 13 or less. This has the effect of [_dominate_](/Spells.aspx?ID=87) and allows a DC 28 Will save. If the aluum is currently under the control of someone wearing its linked charm, its saving throw is one degree higher than what is rolled. You can control only one aluum at a time with this activation, and controlling a new aluum ends the effect for one you had previously affected.

---

A guardian shield is a [steel shield](/Shields.aspx?ID=3) (Hardness 9, HP 36, BT 18) engraved with the symbol of a good deity.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You conjure a Medium guardian with the effects of the [_spiritual guardian_](/Spells.aspx?ID=305) spell, but it carries a shield instead of weapons and can't attack. The guardian appears in an unoccupied space next to an ally of your choice within range and uses the [Raise a Shield](/Actions.aspx?ID=98) action, granting that ally a +2 circumstance bonus to AC until the beginning of your next turn or until your ally is no longer adjacent to the _spiritual guardian_. Each time you Sustain the Activation, the guardian moves to the ally, as long as the ally remains within range, and Raises its Shield, granting its bonus again until the beginning of your next turn or until your ally is no longer adjacent to the _spiritual guardian_. When the ally receiving the AC bonus takes damage beyond the 10 that's redirected to the guardian, you can use a reaction to have the guardian reduce damage for your ally even more by interposing itself further. When it blocks damage in this way, it reduces the damage your ally takes by an additional 20 (for a total of 30 damage reduced), but Dismisses the guardian, immediately ending the activation.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 0+"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Guide](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2469)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Firebrands](/Sources.aspx?ID=196) pg. 93

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Venturing away from home or into the wilderness can be dangerous, especially when the terrain and local creatures are unfamiliar. Guide services reduce the risk of danger during an expedition as guides know the safest or the quickest routes to take through various areas. They also can arrange transportation, food, lodging, and other resources needed for a journey. Guides can assist with locating specific flora or fauna, which is particularly helpful for those in search of ingredients for alchemy or a ritual.

 Guide services typically focus on either wilderness or survival. Wilderness guides are familiar with the terrain and the habits of the creatures who dwell in the region. They can guide you through unfamiliar or hazardous locations using an expedient route, which is the standard route that covers the distance in the shortest amount of time regardless of the hazards you may face, or using a safe route, which doubles your travel time but minimizes the risk of running into [hostile](/Conditions.aspx?ID=23) creatures.

 Survival guides have knowledge of subjects of their level plus 4, so a 1st-level survival guide can help locate targets of up to 5th level. Targets can include creatures, specific plants, or even specific locations such as a glade with a direct view of an upcoming eclipse. The level of a target is either the level of the creature or the level of the challenge used to determine the DC for locating the target, as determined by the GM. For example, the GM might determine that finding a suitable glade would be a challenge for 6th-level characters and require a 2nd-level survival guide to locate. A survival guide can locate a target of their level or lower in 1 day, adding 1 additional day for each level that the target is above the guide's own level.

 Guides typically specialize in particular locations, regions, or routes. If you plan to hire a guide, you must hire one for the appropriate task at hand. The GM can decide that an appropriate guide is unavailable in a given location, requiring you to look elsewhere. For example, you're unlikely to find a guide in Magnimar who can take you across the Wall of Heaven in Tian Xia, but you're likely to find a guide in Goka with the requisite knowledge and experience to do so. Particularly harsh regions or obscure targets might have increased costs, up to 10 times the normal price for their services. Dangerous locales or rare targets may be outside the capabilities of a guide and are best reserved as something that PCs must handle themselves. Organizations like the Firebrands sometimes set up their own guiding services, most notably to assist refugees in crossing remote or dangerous locations. Firebrands may also hire guides to aid in finding specific locations, plants, or creatures in a locale.

For example, the GM might determine that finding a suitable glade would be a challenge for 6th-level characters and require a 2nd-level survival guide to locate. A survival guide can locate a target of their level or lower in 1 day, adding 1 additional day for each level that the target is above the guide's own level.

 Guides typically specialize in particular locations, regions, or routes. If you plan to hire a guide, you must hire one for the appropriate task at hand. The GM can decide that an appropriate guide is unavailable in a given location, requiring you to look elsewhere. For example, you're unlikely to find a guide in Magnimar who can take you across the Wall of Heaven in Tian Xia, but you're likely to find a guide in Goka with the requisite knowledge and experience to do so. Particularly harsh regions or obscure targets might have increased costs, up to 10 times the normal price for their services. Dangerous locales or rare targets may be outside the capabilities of a guide and are best reserved as something that PCs must handle themselves. Organizations like the Firebrands sometimes set up their own guiding services, most notably to assist refugees in crossing remote or dangerous locations. Firebrands may also hire guides to aid in finding specific locations, plants, or creatures in a locale.

This wooden, box-shaped percussion instrument resonates with great power when struck. The drum is large enough that you can't play it while holding it. Instead, you sit on the drum and play it with both hands. Sitting on or standing up from the drum requires an action, which has the [move](/Traits.aspx?ID=114) trait. You're [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16) while sitting on the drum, but you gain a +1 item bonus to [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks to play the drum. The drum is loud and creatures within 100 feet of the drum can hear its music, regardless of the ambient noise, though it can't penetrate [_silence_](/Spells.aspx?ID=287) and similar magical effects.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact ([auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [enchantment](/Traits.aspx?ID=61), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)) **Frequency** once per round;   **Effect** You play the drum, unleashing a rhythm that gets other moving. Up to 2 allies that can hear the drum can use a reaction to Stride 5 feet.

>
[Guiding Chisel](/Equipment.aspx?ID=541)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Age of Ashes</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Elf" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=58" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #148: Fires of the Haunted City](/Sources.aspx?ID=13) pg. 76

**Price** 10,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This magical chisel evokes the holy symbol of the elven goddess of art and architecture, Findeladlara. The _Guiding Chisel’s_ original function was as a portal key to Duskgate, but as Alseta’s Ring faded from the collective memories of the elves, the chisel became known and used exclusively for its other abilities. Eventually, elven emissaries gave it to the dwarves of Saggorak as a gesture of friendship.

 You gain a +3 item bonus to Crafting checks related to stonemasonry. In addition, it takes you only 1 day to Craft items using the _Guiding Chisel_ instead of 4 days, and you quadruple the discount you get for spending additional days Crafting items with the _Guiding Chisel_. If it’s unclear whether you could use the _Guiding Chisel_ to Craft an item, the GM decides.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 10 minutes (command, envision, Interact);  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You embed the _Guiding Chisel_ in the ground and imagine a building. After 10 minutes, you remove the chisel and the building appears. The building can take any shape you wish, filling up to ten contiguous 10-foot cubes within 1,000 feet of the chisel. The building lasts until you use the chisel to create another building. This building has the [structure](/Traits.aspx?ID=153) trait.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

This _+1 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [returning](/Equipment.aspx?ID=301) [starknife](/Weapons.aspx?ID=44)_ is made of dark blue metal overlaid with smoky flecks of fused quartz. When you Cast an [evocation](/Traits.aspx?ID=65) Spell, your next attack this turn with this starknife reduces the target's cover, changing greater cover to standard cover or ignoring standard and lesser cover.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> envision;  **Frequency** once per 10 minutes; **Trigger** You successfully Strike a creature with a [thrown](/Traits.aspx?ID=195) Strike with _guiding star_;  **Effect** Soft light outlines the target. At the beginning of your next turn, the _guiding star's_ blades detach and form into darts of starlight, flying up to 40 feet and striking the target unerringly, collectively dealing 4 piercing damage and 1 good damage before re-forming. The piercing damage increases to 6 with a _greater striking rune_ and 8 with a _major striking rune_.

>
[Guiding Star Orb](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3699)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Spore War</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #211: The Secret of Deathstalk Tower](/Sources.aspx?ID=254) pg. 81

**Price** 6,500 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Candlaron the Sculptor is one of Kyonin’s most storied and honored wizards. While his final fate is unknown, his greatest creations, the aiudara, remain behind as a legacy of his power—as do other potent items, such as the _Guiding Star Orb_, a navigational traveling aid that the heroic wizard often relied upon when venturing into an unexplored part of the world.

**Activate—Embed Location** <actions string="" /> 10 minutes ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))    **Effect** By focusing on the _Guiding Star Orb_, you embed your current location in the item. Thereafter, anyone who holds the _Guiding Star Orb_ while [Casting a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) with the [teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=710) trait to travel to this location arrives precisely, without any inaccuracy at all. The _Guiding Star Orb_ can only have one location embedded at a time; if you use this activity a second time, the new location replaces the previous one.

**Activate—Momentary Aiudara** <actions string="" /> 10 minutes ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=710)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You cause a shimmering magical archway to appear next to you as the _Guiding Star Orb_ casts a 7th-rank [_teleport_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1720) to your specifications. If you are teleporting to an aiudara you’ve visited before, you and the targets appear precisely at that location.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

fields.text: Item 7 Guiding Starknife Divine Source Impossible Magic pg. 209 Price 325 gp Usage held in 1 hand Bulk L Base Weapon Starknife This +1 striking returning starknife is made of dark blue metal overlaid with smoky flecks of fused quartz. When you Cast a Spell and deal damage, your next attack before the end of your turn with this starknife ignores standard and lesser cover. Activate—Points of Light Reaction (concentrate, spirit) Frequency once per 10 minutes; Trigger You successfully Strike a creature with a thrown Strike with the guiding starknife ; Requirements ; Effect The guiding starknife ’s blades detach, form into darts of starlight, and deal 4 piercing damage plus 1d4 spirit damage to the creature you just hit. This piercing damage increases to 6 with a greater striking rune and to 8 with a major striking rune. The guiding starknife then re-forms and returns to your hand. Until the start of your next turn, the damaged creature is outlined with soft light and can’t gain the effects of concealment.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 3"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Gunner's Bandolier](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1209)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 179

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) Characters with access to firearms gain access to accessories that can be used with those weapons._

**Price** 60 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This incredibly spacious bandolier can hold up to 4 one-handed crossbows or firearms that take no more than 1 action to completely reload (typically meaning that weapons with the [capacity](/Traits.aspx?ID=399) or [repeating](/Traits.aspx?ID=374) traits won't fit in the bandolier's holsters). A _gunner's bandolier_ can be etched with runes as though it were a ranged weapon. When you invest the _gunner's bandolier_, you can attune it to each of the 4 weapons holstered in it.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))    **Effect** You empower one of the attuned weapons in the bandolier, granting it the runes etched onto the _gunner's bandolier_ and removing the runes from any previously drawn weapon. Then, you Interact to draw the weapon.

**Activate** <actions string="Three Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))    **Effect** All weapons that were attuned to the bandolier when you invested it, not including any weapons you're currently wielding, return to the bandolier, and one of the returned weapons is automatically reloaded.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

    level="1"
    right="Item 2"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Gunner's Saddle](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1217)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 182

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) Characters with access to firearms gain access to accessories that can be used with those weapons._

**Price** 20 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn saddle

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Developed by marauders from the Mana Wastes, this clockwork saddle comes with a retractable weapon mount that can be used as a [tripod](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1207) to stabilize a weapon with the [kickback](/Traits.aspx?ID=409) trait. Just like a normal tripod, you Interact to deploy the tripod to stabilize the firearm, and then again to retract the tripod to move it. The saddle uses complex hydraulics to protect the steed from the firearm's recoil.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

This _+1 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2829) [ogre hook](/Weapons.aspx?ID=495)_ causes its owner to dream of past murders conducted with the weapon. _Gut-Ripper's_ mythic magic is tied to the bloodlust of the [ogre boss](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3120) who was holding it upon becoming mythic. If _Gut-Ripper_ doesn't kill a creature each day by midnight, it becomes a non-magical ogre hook.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Rip Guts! Rip Guts!; **Cost** 1 Mythic Point;    **Effect** You throw _Gut-Ripper_ in a line of any length up to 60 feet, then it returns to your hands. Each creature in the line takes 2d10 piercing damage with a DC 25 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save. If there's a creature at the end of the line, you instead make a melee Strike against it with the hook that deals an additional 2d10 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29). Each time a creature takes this bleed damage, you regain that many HP; this is a [healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=623) [vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509) effect. This activation can't be used again for 1d4 rounds.

---

A _gyroscopic stabilizer_ appears as a gold disk suspended within three rotating golden bands inside a gilded case, itself attached to a set of clamps. These clamps allow you to attach the _gyroscopic stabilizer_ to any one-handed firearm as an Interact action.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per hour;  **Requirements** The _gyroscopic stabilizer_ is attached to a one-handed firearm without the [fatal](/Traits.aspx?ID=178) or [fatal aim](/Traits.aspx?ID=404) traits; **Effect** The gyroscopic stabilizer begins spinning for 1 minute. While the gyroscopic stabilizer is spinning, the weapon it's attached to gains the fatal aim weapon trait with a die one size larger than its damage die (maximum d12). This allows you to wield it in two hands to grant it the fatal trait.

Long associated with a notorious crime boss in Nantambu, this stout _+1 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [fearsome](/Equipment.aspx?ID=731) [club](/Weapons.aspx?ID=2)_ is studded with vicious-looking knobs of obsidian and wrapped in cloth for a better grip. It emits a ghastly groan when swung.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You gesture at a square within 40 feet with _Habu's Cudgel_. **Source** [Bestiary 3](/Sources.aspx?ID=66) pg. 128 **Usage** worn --- This item appears to be an ordinary semiprecious stone and is typically mounted on a brooch or ring, but the stone is, in fact, an eyeball. This illusion can be seen through with [_true seeing_](/Spells.aspx?ID=344) or similar magic, and anyone who interacts with the item feels its wet and sticky surface, allowing them to attempt to [disbelieve](/Rules.aspx?ID=267) the illusion (DC 19). Many hags claim a _hag eye_ is more effective if plucked from a living, awake creature, but this is likely just a convenient excuse for sadism. The _hag eye_ produces no direct benefit for the wearer, but allows the [hag](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=59) who created it, or any member of her coven, can peer through the eye using the [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=84) action. This has no range limit, provided the hag is on the same plane. Any damage dealt to the eye destroys it. If this happens while a hag is looking through it, the hag is [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=1) for 1 hour. **Craft Requirements** You must be a hag. Hag Eye **Source** [Bestiary 3](/Sources.aspx?ID=66) pg. 128 **Price** 50 gp **Usage** worn Hag Eye (Frightful) **Source** [Pathfinder #182: Graveclaw](/Sources.aspx?ID=143) pg. 76 **Price** 85 gp **Usage** worn --- A _frightful hag eye_ is made with the eye of a creature whose gaze inflicts fear, such as some velstracs. **Activate** ([emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [enchantment](/Traits.aspx?ID=61), [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=68), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163)) **Trigger** once per day; **Effect** You target a creature within 30 feet that must be able to see the _frightful hag eye_; the target must attempt a DC 19 Will save. Once a creature attempts this save, it's temporarily immune for 24 hours. **Critical Success** The target is unaffected.
**Success** The target is [frightened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19).
**Failure** The target is frightened 2.
**Critical Failure** The target is frightened 3 and [fleeing](/Conditions.aspx?ID=17) for 1 round. Hag Eye (Oracular) **Source** [Pathfinder #182: Graveclaw](/Sources.aspx?ID=143) pg. 76 **Price** 75 gp **Usage** worn **Bulk** L --- _Oracular hag eyes_ are made with the eye of a [cyclops](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=25). A hag who casts [_augury_](/Spells.aspx?ID=15) with an _oracular hag eye_ in her possession reduces the DC of the secret flat check to 2. Hag Eye (Smokey) **Source** [Pathfinder #182: Graveclaw](/Sources.aspx?ID=143) pg. 76 **Price** 450 gp **Usage** worn --- A _smoky hag eye_ is named after the black vapor that constantly emanates from it, like the smoke that continually seeps from a [bodak's](/Monsters.aspx?ID=573) eye. **Activate** ([death](/Traits.aspx?ID=40), [necromancy](/Traits.aspx?ID=117), [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163)) **Effect** You target a creature within 30 feet that must be able to see the _smoky hag eye_. The target must attempt a DC 24 Fortitude save. Once a creature attempts this save, it's temporarily immune for 24 hours. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature is [drained 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=10).
**Failure** The creature is [doomed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=9) and drained 2.
**Critical Failure** The creature is doomed 1 and drained 3. Hag Eye (Stoney) **Source** [Pathfinder #182: Graveclaw](/Sources.aspx?ID=143) pg. 76 **Price** 250 gp **Usage** worn --- A _stony hag eye_ is fashioned from the eye of a creature, such a [basilisk](/Monsters.aspx?ID=44) or [medusa](/Monsters.aspx?ID=297), with a petrifying gaze. **Activate** ([incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=93), [transmutation](/Traits.aspx?ID=157), [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163)) **Trigger** once per round; **Effect** You target a creature within 30 feet that can see the _stony hag eye_. The target must attempt a DC 22 Fortitude save. On a failure, it's [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35) for 1 minute; on a critical failure, if the creature is already slowed, it's permanently [petrified](/Conditions.aspx?ID=30). Touching the _stony hag eye_ to the petrified creature (a single action with the [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104) trait) removes the petrified condition.

    level="1"
    right="Item 3"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Hagbane Biscuit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=4950)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Troubles in Grayce</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=528" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=564" />
<trait label="Processed" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=487" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Sweet Tooth](/Sources.aspx?ID=332) pg. 87, [Troubles in Grayce](/Sources.aspx?ID=327) pg. 87

**Price** 10 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This gingerbread biscuit is stamped in the shape of a menacing witch, her features decorated with anise and fennel seeds. When you eat the biscuit, its sharp spices warm your body for 10 minutes, granting you a +1 status bonus [Perception](/Rules.aspx?ID=2040) checks to pierce a [hag’s](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=425) disguise, to skill checks to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) about hags, and to saving throws made against hags’ abilities and spells. During this time, weapons you wield count as [cold iron](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2916) for any physical attacks made against hags. 

The biscuit tastes especially bitter to hags, changelings, and other hag-related creatures (such as a [sorcerer](/Classes.aspx?ID=62) with the [hag bloodline](/Bloodlines.aspx?ID=26)). If such a creature attempts to eat the biscuit, they must succeed at a DC 18 Fortitude save or it fails and wastes the action (and is [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91) 1 on a critical failure).

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

The flower that adorns this hairpin is a blooming lotus flower that varies in color; it regrows in a day after the item is activated. Whether or not the hairpin's flower is in bloom, as long as you wear it and it's invested, it grants a +1 item bonus to Diplomacy checks. 

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You pluck the flower from the hairpin and scatter the petals, creating a flurry of color in a 10-foot burst centered on you. You become concealed for 1 minute or until you move from your current location. Any creature within the 10-foot burst when you Activate the Item must succeed at a DC 23 Reflex save or become [dazzled ](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65) until the end of its next turn (or [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59) until the end of its next turn on a critical failure). The flower blooms again the next day.

Whether or not the hairpin’s flower is in bloom, as long as you wear it and it’s invested, it grants a +1 item bonus to Diplomacy checks. Activate—Scatter Petals Two Actions (concentrate, manipulate) Frequency once per day; Effect You pluck the flower from the hairpin and scatter the petals, creating a flurry of color in a 10-foot burst centered on you. You become concealed for 1 minute or until you move from your current location. Any creature within the 10-foot burst when you Activate the Item must succeed at a DC 23 Reflex save or become dazzled until the end of its next turn (or blinded until the end of its next turn on a critical failure). The flower blooms again the next day.

May contain spoilers from Strength of Thousands **Source** [Pathfinder #174: Shadows of the Ancients](/Sources.aspx?ID=115) pg. 77 **Usage** held in 2 hands **Bulk** 1 --- This shekere features carved prayers barely visible under a fine silk net of colorful beads. The handheld percussion instrument grants a +3 item bonus to [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks while playing music with it. In addition, when you [Perform](/Actions.aspx?ID=59) with it, you can make it heard by any number of creatures within 100 miles. You can specify one or more specific creatures, or otherwise describe those who will hear it, such as all [humans](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=6), or all inhabitants of a village. You can send a message through the music that the targets understand. [Demons](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=28) and creatures connected to demons (such as a creature whose deity is a [demon lord](/DeityCategories.aspx?ID=5) or a [sorcerer](/Classes.aspx?ID=11) with the [demonic bloodline](/Bloodlines.aspx?ID=3)) can't easily understand any messages conveyed in this way, even if you wish to send the message to them. They must attempt a [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) check against your Performance DC or against DC 40, whichever is higher. If your Performance DC is higher than DC 40 and you want demons to be able to understand the message, you can choose to use DC 40 instead. **Success** They understand the message.
**Failure** They don't understand the message but are aware there was one.
**Critical Failure** They don't realize the sound of the _halcyon heart_ contains a message. **Activate** command, Interact; **Requirements** The _halcyon heart_ has its net of beads; **Effect** You pull the net off the _halcyon heart_ and throw it at a creature within 20 feet, using your attack bonus for a ranged simple weapon. On a hit, the net grows and envelops the creature, which becomes [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16) and takes a –10-foot circumstance penalty to its Speeds until it [Escapes](/Actions.aspx?ID=79), and on a critical hit, it's also [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=24) until it Escapes. The net also attempts to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) [teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=156) effects and planar travel of the creature it's entrapping. The Escape DC is 44, and the net has a counteract level of 9 and a counteract modifier of +38. If the target is a demon or connected to a demon, they must roll twice and take the lower result on all attempts to Escape (this is a [misfortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=110) effect), and for counteract checks, the net rolls twice and takes the higher result (this is a [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=76) effect). You can't Perform with the _halcyon heart_ while it doesn't have its net. So long as the net doesn't contain a creature, you can restore it with a single action, which has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32) trait. **Destruction** If the Gorilla King plays a _halcyon heart_ in front of [Angazhan's](/Deities.aspx?ID=72) totem, the gourd decomposes, the net frays, and the beads shatter.

You arrange brambles, wires, sticky goo, or other materials to interfere with a creature’s movement. The square with this snare, as well as three adjacent squares (to form a 10-foot-by-10-foot area), become difficult terrain when the first creature enters the snare’s square. The difficult terrain affects the creature’s movement right away, including its movement into the triggering square, and it lasts for 1d4 rounds after the snare is triggered. A creature can use an Interact action to clear the difficult terrain out of a single square early.

---

At the crossroads under a new moon, you traded your face for one that you can mold as though it were clay, sealed with a ribbon worn around your neck to hide the seam. Your true appearance changes to that of a generic member of your ancestry. You can shape your facial features with your hands and thus don't need a [disguise kit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=19) to [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=46), and you don't take circumstance penalties to Impersonate someone due to the difference in your facial features. Once per day, from any distance, the entity that holds your bargained contract can change their appearance to match your appearance from before you sealed the contract, or the appearance you are currently using through Impersonate. When they do, your face transforms to your new true appearance, that of a generic member of your ancestry, and you become [stunned 3](/Conditions.aspx?ID=36) by the sudden backlash.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact;    **Requirements** You have used Impersonate and molded your face into a different face; **Effect** You peel your current face from your skin, revealing the true generic appearance from your bargained contract. This allows you to duck out of sight and remove the facial component of your disguise almost immediately, though clothing or other elements might still give you away.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

Your true appearance changes to that of a generic member of your ancestry. You can shape your facial features with your hands and thus don't need a disguise kit to Impersonate, and you don't take circumstance penalties to Impersonate someone due to the difference in your facial features. Once per day, from any distance, the entity that holds your bargained contract can change their appearance to match your appearance from before you sealed the contract, or the appearance you're currently using through Impersonate. When they do, your face transforms to your new true appearance—that of a generic member of your ancestry—and you become stunned 3 by the sudden backlash. Activate—Fresh Face Two Actions (manipulate) Requirements You have used Impersonate and molded your face into a different face.; Effect You peel your current face from your skin, revealing the true generic appearance from your bargained contract . This allows you to duck out of sight and remove the facial component of your disguise almost immediately, though clothing or other elements might still give you away.

>
[Handcuffs](/Equipment.aspx?ID=798)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Agents of Edgewatch</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #157: Devil at the Dreaming Palace](/Sources.aspx?ID=45) pg. 77

<row gap="medium">

**Hands** 1

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Developed in Absalom and rarely used except by police forces in major cities due to their significant cost, handcuffs possess a ratcheting lock system in each cuff that allows them to be quickly cinched down on a captive's limbs, even if they're actively resisting.

 To apply handcuffs, you must first grab or restrain your opponent, then attempt an [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) check against the opponent's Fortitude DC. On a success, you lock one of the cuffs around your opponent's wrist. You can lock the other cuff to yourself or a stationary object within reach as an Interact action; to lock it to another creature (either the same opponent you just cuffed or a separate creature altogether), you must first grab or restrain that creature, as before, and then make an Athletics check against its Fortitude DC. The DC to make the Athletics check against your own wrist is 5, or 10 for an unattended object.

 If you bind a creature to itself, it takes the same penalties as those imposed by [manacles](/Equipment.aspx?ID=32). If you bind a creature to another creature (including yourself), the two creatures are locked together and must remain in adjacent spaces, and both creatures gain the [clumsy 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=3) condition as long as they are handcuffed. If you lock a creature to an immobile object, such as a bar or tree, the creature is [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=24). (For creatures with an unusual physiology such as more or fewer limbs, the GM determines what effects handcuffs have, if any.)

 Handcuffs are unlocked via a key and are easier to slip out of than ordinary manacles. The chain between handcuffs can be Broken Open with a single Athletics check.

fields.text: Item 3+ Handcuffs May contain spoilers from Agents of Edgewatch Uncommon Source Pathfinder #157: Devil at the Dreaming Palace pg. 77 Hands 1 Usage held in 1 hand Bulk L Developed in Absalom and rarely used except by police forces in major cities due to their significant cost, handcuffs possess a ratcheting lock system in each cuff that allows them to be quickly cinched down on a captive's limbs, even if they're actively resisting. To apply handcuffs, you must first grab or restrain your opponent, then attempt an Athletics check against the opponent's Fortitude DC. On a success, you lock one of the cuffs around your opponent's wrist. You can lock the other cuff to yourself or a stationary object within reach as an Interact action; to lock it to another creature (either the same opponent you just cuffed or a separate creature altogether), you must first grab or restrain that creature, as before, and then make an Athletics check against its Fortitude DC. The DC to make the Athletics check against your own wrist is 5, or 10 for an unattended object. If you bind a creature to itself, it takes the same penalties as those imposed by manacles. If you bind a creature to another creature (including yourself), the two creatures are locked together and must remain in adjacent spaces, and both creatures gain the clumsy 1 condition as long as they are handcuffed. If you lock a creature to an immobile object, such as a bar or tree, the creature is immobilized. (For creatures with an unusual physiology such as more or fewer limbs, the GM determines what effects handcuffs have, if any.) Handcuffs are unlocked via a key and are easier to slip out of than ordinary manacles. The chain between handcuffs can be Broken Open with a single Athletics check. Item 3 Handcuffs (Average) Source Pathfinder #157: Devil at the Dreaming Palace pg. 77 Price 30 gp Bulk L Escaping requires two successful DC 27 Thievery checks, and the Athletics DC to Break Open the chain between handcuffs is 30. Item 9 Handcuffs (Good) Source Pathfinder #157: Devil at the Dreaming Palace pg. 77 Price 350 gp Bulk L Escaping requires three successful DC 30 Thievery checks, and the Athletics DC to Break Open the chain between handcuffs is 35. Item 17 Handcuffs (Superior) Source Pathfinder #157: Devil at the Dreaming Palace pg. 77 Price 6,000 gp Bulk L Escaping requires four successful DC 40 Thievery checks, and the Athletics DC to Break Open the chain between handcuffs is 45.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Cursed" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=274" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 191

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn headwear

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This elegant scarf appears to be and functions as a [_masquerade scarf_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3095). When you invest the scarf, it fuses to you.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 1 minute ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** Like a _masquerade scarf_, the scarf casts a 1st-rank [_illusory disguise_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1568) spell on you. However, the illusion disadvantages you based on your intent, making you, for example, appear to be a suspicious ruffian if you’re trying to sneak past guards or lending you the seeming of a pauper if you’re trying to impress a shallow aristocrat. You and those you consider to be allies must succeed at a DC 16 Will save or you perceive the [illusion](/Rules.aspx?ID=267) as you intended it, though others won’t. Evidence to the contrary allows you to attempt to disbelieve the false version of the illusion. You can’t Dismiss the spell.

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 2+"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Handwraps of Mighty Blows](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3086)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=637" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 290

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn gloves

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Fist](/Weapons.aspx?ID=356)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

As you invest these embroidered strips of cloth, you must meditate and slowly wrap them around your hands. These handwraps have weapon runes etched into them to give your unarmed attacks the benefits of those runes, making your unarmed attacks work like magic weapons. For example, _+1 striking handwraps of mighty blows_ would give you a +1 item bonus to attack rolls with your unarmed attacks and increase the damage of your unarmed attacks from one weapon die to two (normally 2d4 instead of 1d4, but if your fists have a different weapon damage die or you have other unarmed attacks, use two of that die size instead).

 You can upgrade, add, and transfer runes to and from the handwraps just as you would for a weapon, and you can attach talismans to the handwraps. Treat the handwraps as melee weapons of the brawling group with light Bulk for these purposes. Property runes apply only when they would be applicable to the unarmed attack you're using. For example, a property that must be applied to a slashing weapon wouldn't function when you attacked with a fist, but you would gain its benefits if you attacked with a claw or some other slashing unarmed attack.

 The entries below list the most typical combinations of fundamental runes.

fields.text: Item 0 Handwraps of Mighty Blows Invested Magical Transmutation Source Core Rulebook pg. 611 Usage worn gloves As you invest these embroidered strips of cloth, you must meditate and slowly wrap them around your hands. These handwraps have weapon runes etched into them to give your unarmed attacks the benefits of those runes, making your unarmed attacks work like magic weapons. For example, +1 striking handwraps of mighty blows would give you a +1 item bonus to attack rolls with your unarmed attacks and increase the damage of your unarmed attacks from one weapon die to two (normally 2d4 instead of 1d4, but if your fists have a different weapon damage die or you have other unarmed attacks, use two of that die size instead). You can upgrade, add, and transfer runes to and from the handwraps just as you would for a weapon, and you can attach talismans to the handwraps. Treat the handwraps as melee weapons of the brawling group with light Bulk for these purposes. Property runes apply only when they would be applicable to the unarmed attack you’re using. For example, a property that must be applied to a slashing weapon wouldn’t function when you attacked with a fist, but you would gain its benefits if you attacked with a claw or some other slashing unarmed attack. The entries below list the most typical combinations of fundamental runes.

 You can upgrade, add, and transfer runes to and from the handwraps just as you would for a weapon, and you can attach talismans to the handwraps. Treat the handwraps as melee weapons of the brawling group with light Bulk for these purposes. Property runes apply only when they would be applicable to the unarmed attack you're using. For example, a property that must be applied to a slashing weapon wouldn't function when you attacked with a fist, but you would gain its benefits if you attacked with a claw or some other slashing unarmed attack.

As you invest these embroidered strips of cloth, you must meditate and slowly wrap them around your hands. These handwraps have weapon runes etched into them to give your unarmed attacks the benefits of those runes, making your unarmed attacks work like magic weapons. For example, _+1 striking handwraps of mighty blows_ would give you a +1 item bonus to attack rolls with your unarmed attacks and increase the damage of your unarmed attacks from one weapon die to two (normally 2d4 instead of 1d4, but if your fists have a different weapon damage die or you have other unarmed attacks, use two of that die size instead).

 You can upgrade, add, and transfer runes to and from the handwraps just as you would for a weapon, and you can attach talismans to the handwraps. Treat the handwraps as melee weapons of the brawling group with light Bulk for these purposes. Property runes apply only when they would be applicable to the unarmed attack you're using. For example, a property that must be applied to a slashing weapon wouldn't function when you attacked with a fist, but you would gain its benefits if you attacked with a claw or some other slashing unarmed attack.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 14"
    pfs=""
>
[Hardened Harrow Deck](/Equipment.aspx?ID=837)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Agents of Edgewatch</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #160: Assault on Hunting Lodge Seven](/Sources.aspx?ID=49) pg. 66

**Price** 4,350 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Dart](/Weapons.aspx?ID=68)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The harrow is a traditional fortunetelling deck used by Varisian soothsayers. The _hardened harrow deck_ is a magical version of the deck with cards made of thin metallic plates adorned with all the imagery common in standard harrow decks, but with more angular designs. You can hurl cards from the hardened harrow deck as _+2 [greater striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [darts](/Weapons.aspx?ID=68)_ with the [deadly d10](/Traits.aspx?ID=174) trait. A card used as a weapon isn't destroyed and can be recovered with 1 minute of searching if it can't be recalled back to the deck (see the deck's Activate entry below). However, if even a single card is missing from the deck, the deck can't be used to perform a traditional harrow reading.

 As long as you carry more than half the cards in the _hardened harrow deck_, when you roll a success on a saving throw against a [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=68) effect, you get a critical success instead; if you already have an ability that would make a successful saving throw against a fear effect a critical success, you instead gain a +1 circumstance bonus to saving throws against fear effects.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> command, Interact;     **Effect** All cards from the _hardened harrow deck_ within 60 feet that you can see fly back into the deck.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 13"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Harmonic Hauberk](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1380)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Auditory" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=16" />
<trait label="Focused" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=74" />
<trait label="Illusion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=92" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 84

**Price** 2,500 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn armor

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Armor** [Chain Shirt](/Armor.aspx?ID=6)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Rose gold and copper rings in this _+2 [resilient](/Equipment.aspx?ID=279) [chain shirt](/Armor.aspx?ID=6)_ form a vague bird shape. The jingling links tinkle musically, almost like birdsong. While you wear the armor, effects with the [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16) trait must first [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) the _harmonic hauberk_ or they have no effect on you.

 The _harmonic hauberk_ attempts to counteract [_silence_](/Spells.aspx?ID=287) spells cast on you and 4th-level or higher heightened _silence_ spells the first time the armor enters their area (counteract level 4, counteract modifier +20). After failing to counteract a _silence_ spell, the armor can't attempt to counteract the same spell again, even if you leave and enter the spell's area multiple times.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> command;  **Frequency** once per day;  **Requirements** You have a pool of Focus Points and at least one [composition](/Traits.aspx?ID=31) spell; **Effect** You gain 1 Focus Point and immediately use the Focus Point to cast [_lingering composition_](/Spells.aspx?ID=389), using your [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) check to determine the effects of the spell, followed by the [_inspire defense_](/Spells.aspx?ID=387) composition cantrip. You can use this activation to cast those spells even if you don't have the [Lingering Composition](/Feats.aspx?ID=180) or [Inspire Defense](/Feats.aspx?ID=188) feats.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

fields.text: Item 13 Harmonic Hauberk Uncommon Auditory Focused Illusion Invested Magical Source Grand Bazaar pg. 84 Price 2,500 gp Usage worn armor Bulk 1 Base Armor Chain Shirt Rose gold and copper rings in this +2 resilient chain shirt form a vague bird shape. The jingling links tinkle musically, almost like birdsong. While you wear the armor, effects with the auditory trait must first counteract the harmonic hauberk or they have no effect on you. The harmonic hauberk attempts to counteract silence spells cast on you and 4th-level or higher heightened silence spells the first time the armor enters their area (counteract level 4, counteract modifier +20). After failing to counteract a silence spell, the armor can't attempt to counteract the same spell again, even if you leave and enter the spell's area multiple times. Activate Single Action command; Frequency once per day; Requirements You have a pool of Focus Points and at least one composition spell; Effect You gain 1 Focus Point and immediately use the Focus Point to cast lingering composition , using your Performance check to determine the effects of the spell, followed by the inspire defense composition cantrip. You can use this activation to cast those spells even if you don't have the Lingering Composition or Inspire Defense feats.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 4"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Harpoon Bolt](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1589)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Outlaws of Alkenstar</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #179: Cradle of Quartz](/Sources.aspx?ID=122) pg. 77

**Price** 15 gp

<row gap="medium">
**Ammunition** round

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This iron spike can be fitted into the barrel of a two-handed [firearm](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=16) that doesn't have the [scatter](/Traits.aspx?ID=413) property with an Interact action. The spike is attached to a 50-foot-long coil of rope held in a simple spool that can be attached to a weapon's barrel. The weight and awkward balance of the bolt and its spool reduce the [range](/Traits.aspx?ID=248) of the weapon by 10 feet when fired. A creature hit by a _harpoon bolt_ takes normal damage from the shot and must succeed at a DC 18 Fortitude save. On a failure, the _harpoon bolt_ becomes lodged in its body.

Once a _harpoon bolt_ is lodged, a creature can remove the harpoon bolt with a DC 18 check to [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=79) or [Force Open](/Actions.aspx?ID=34), but on a failure, the creature takes 1d4 piercing damage. As long as the _harpoon bolt_ remains lodged, the creature can't move more than 50 feet away from you. You can attempt to [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=40) a creature by tugging on the rope attached to the harpoon bolt, even if it isn't within your reach, but if you fail this attempt, the bolt rips free, causing 1d4 piercing damage to the target but releasing it from the bolt. If you reload, drop, or fire the firearm again, the creature is no longer limited in its movement. Once a _harpoon bolt_ is removed from a creature, the bolt, its rope, and the spool all decay away, consumed by the same magic that empowers the unusual ammunition to function in the first place.

</column>

</title>

<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
<trait label="Talisman" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=709" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #222: Hellbreakers](/Sources.aspx?ID=307) pg. 210

**Price** 3 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** affixed to a slashing weapon

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Free Action" /><row>([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32))</row></row>

---

This sharp metal claw is used to inflict additional pain upon your enemies. When you activate the _harpy's talon_, the weapon deals [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) equal to the number of weapon damage dice. If the Strike was a critical success, the persistent bleed damage increases to twice the number of weapon damage dice.

Used by gamblers and seers alike, this deck of cards comes in several varieties. Simple harrow decks are made from low-quality paper and typically have only an icon and a number to signify the suit and alignment. These simple decks are mostly used for games of chance, as the actual image and significance of the cards are irrelevant for such games. Common harrow decks are made from higher-quality paper and feature illustrations—harrow readers typically use these decks. Fine harrow decks are made from a variety of materials, such as high-quality paper, woods, bone, ivory, or metal.

fields.text: Item 0+ Harrow Deck Source Pathfinder #160: Assault on Hunting Lodge Seven pg. 66 Hands 2 Bulk L Used by gamblers and seers alike, this deck of cards comes in several varieties. Simple harrow decks are made from low-quality paper and typically have only an icon and a number to signify the suit and alignment. These simple decks are mostly used for games of chance, as the actual image and significance of the cards are irrelevant for such games. Common harrow decks are made from higher-quality paper and feature illustrations—harrow readers typically use these decks. Fine harrow decks are made from a variety of materials, such as high-quality paper, woods, bone, ivory, or metal. [Harrow Spellcards](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2178)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Grimoire" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=387" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 112

**Price** 425 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Crafted of sturdy paper, each card of this [harrow deck](/Equipment.aspx?ID=824) showcases a beautiful watercolor illustration with space to inscribe a spell below. When shuffled, its cards seem to fly between one another of their own accord.

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** Your last action was to cast a spell prepared from this grimoire that has the [detection](/Traits.aspx?ID=574), [prediction](/Traits.aspx?ID=674), [revelation](/Traits.aspx?ID=686), or [scrying](/Traits.aspx?ID=689) trait;  **Effect** You draw forth a card to gain insight into future challenges you’ll face. Draw a card from a harrow deck or roll 1d6: 1 = hammers ([Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36)), 2 = keys ([Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34)), 3 = shields ([Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49)), 4 = books (any [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367)), 5 = stars ([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)), 6 = crowns ([Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39)). The next time you attempt a check of the same type as your result, roll twice and take the better result, as the spirits of the harrow guide your actions. If not used by your next [daily preparations](/Rules.aspx?ID=2575), this benefit disappears.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Cursed" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=274" />
<trait label="Illusion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=92" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault](/Sources.aspx?ID=320) pg. 191

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn headwear

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This elegant hat appears to be and functions as a _[hat of disguise](/Equipment.aspx?ID=442)_. When you invest the hat, it fuses to you.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 1 minute (Interact);  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** Like a _hat of disguise_, the hat casts a 1st-level [_illusory disguise_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1568) spell on you. However, the illusion disadvantages you based on your intent, making you, for example, appear to be a suspicious ruffian if you’re trying to sneak past guards or lending you the seeming of a pauper if you’re trying to impress a shallow aristocrat. You and those you consider to be allies must succeed at a DC 16 Will save or you perceive the illusion as you intended it, though others won’t. Evidence to the contrary allows you to attempt to disbelieve the false version of the illusion. You can’t [Dismiss](/Actions.aspx?ID=2311) the spell.

Evidence to the contrary allows you to attempt to disbelieve the false version of the illusion. You can’t Dismiss the spell. </title>

<traits>
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 185

**Price** 1,800 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn headwear

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This pointy, brimmed hat made up of a rainbow patchwork of various materials seems to sit just a little lopsided on your head, no matter how you adjust it. You gain a +2 item bonus to checks to [Earn Income](/Actions.aspx?ID=23).

**Activate** <actions string="Three Actions" /> envision, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You tear off a patch of cloth to manifest it into a copy of yourself, dressed in the color and fabric of the patch. The copy follows your specific instructions and performs a single, straightforward task for up to 30 minutes. It takes the copy three times as long to complete the task as it would you, meaning it can perform a task that would take you a maximum of 10 minutes. It doesn't react quickly enough to be of any use during an encounter, and it can't use your spells or other special abilities—just basic actions and skill actions.

 The copy disappears and returns to the hat as a piece of cloth when the given task has been completed, or when you Dismiss the activation.

It takes the copy three times as long to complete the task as it would you, meaning it can perform a task that would take you a maximum of 10 minutes. It doesn’t react quickly enough to be of any use during an encounter, and it can’t use your spells or other special abilities—just basic actions and skill actions. [Headband of Inspired Wisdom](/Equipment.aspx?ID=402)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Abjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=2" />
<trait label="Apex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=10" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 604

**Price** 15,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn circlet

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This simple cloth headband remains pristine and clean at all times, no matter the circumstances. When you invest the headband, you either increase your Wisdom score by 2 or increase it to 18, whichever would give you a higher score.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> envision;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** When you are considering a course of action, you get a gut feeling about whether it’s a good idea. You gain the effects of an [_augury_](/Spells.aspx?ID=15) spell, except that you receive the result from your own instincts rather than an external source.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> envision (fortune);  **Frequency** once per hour; **Trigger** You fail a saving throw against an effect that makes you confused, fascinated, or stupefied;  **Effect** The _headband of inspired wisdom_ clears your mind. You can reroll the saving throw and use the better result.

>
[Headbands of Translocation](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2336)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Teleportation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=156" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 152, [Pathfinder #167: Ready? Fight!](/Sources.aspx?ID=86) pg. 74

**Price** 10,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn headwear

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

_Headbands of translocation_ are silk bands that come in pairs and usually feature a prominent symbol of a nation or team. If both wearers Invest their headbands at the same time and think of the same symbol while doing so, both headbands change to display that symbol until they are removed. If you both have invested your headbands, you can [Aid](/Actions.aspx?ID=75) each other without taking an action to prepare, and when you roll a critical failure when attempting to Aid an ally with a paired headband, you get a failure instead.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You remove your headband, which teleports you to a space adjacent to the other Invested wearer's location, provided you are within 1 mile of each other.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 54

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Three Actions" /><row>([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Healing vapor is a substance that accelerates natural recovery processes by dispersing a mist infused with a variety of reagents typically used for healing and recovery. When deployed from a sealed container, the vapors fill a 5-foot burst, last for 10 minutes, and can affect up to four living creatures at one time. Any creatures beyond the first four gain no benefit, though if a creature leaves before the duration is over, a new creature that enters can benefit from the mist. A creature benefiting from the vapors regains a number of Hit Points based on the vapor's type. While affected, a creature also gains an item bonus to saving throws against diseases and poisons. If the areas of more than one healing vapor overlap, only the strongest applies to creatures inside overlapping areas. Strong wind disperses the mist, rendering it ineffective while the wind blows.

---

Healing vapor is a substance that accelerates natural recovery processes by dispersing a mist infused with a variety of reagents typically used for healing and recovery. When deployed from a sealed container, the vapors fill a 5-foot burst, last for 10 minutes, and can affect up to four living creatures at one time. Any creatures beyond the first four gain no benefit, though if a creature leaves before the duration is over, a new creature that enters can benefit from the mist. A creature benefiting from the vapors regains a number of Hit Points based on the vapor's type. While affected, a creature also gains an item bonus to saving throws against diseases and poisons. If the areas of more than one healing vapor overlap, only the strongest applies to creatures inside overlapping areas. Strong wind disperses the mist, rendering it ineffective while the wind blows.

A hearing aid is worn in the ear and is made from carved wood, shaped metal, or even small clockwork pieces. The shape of the device aids those who are hard of hearing, and you can wear one or two depending on your hearing loss. You can attach or remove your hearing aids as an Interact action.

</traits>

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 293

**Price** 5 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

A magical hearing aid has the [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103) trait. With its curved shape, it hooks over the top and sits behind your ear, with a receiver that fits into the ear opening. The external part of the device detects sound waves and, using magic, transfers them down the receiver and into your ear. You can wear one or two depending on your hearing loss, and you can turn your hearing aids on or off using an Interact action.

fields.text: Item 0+ Hearing Aid Source Player Core pg. 293 A hearing aid is worn in the ear and is made from carved wood, shaped metal, or even small clockwork pieces. The shape of the device aids those who are hard of hearing, and you can wear one or two depending on your hearing loss. You can attach or remove your hearing aids as an Interact action. Item 0 Hearing Aid Source Player Core pg. 293 Price 5 sp Item 0 Hearing Aid (Magical) Source Player Core pg. 293 Price 5 gp A magical hearing aid has the magical trait. With its curved shape, it hooks over the top and sits behind your ear, with a receiver that fits into the ear opening. The external part of the device detects sound waves and, using magic, transfers them down the receiver and into your ear. You can wear one or two depending on your hearing loss, and you can turn your hearing aids on or off using an Interact action.

>
[Heart Bloodstone of Arazni](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3783)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Claws of the Tyrant</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=253" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=48" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Claws of the Tyrant](/Sources.aspx?ID=266) pg. 109

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The _Heart Bloodstone of Arazni_ represents protection. While holding the _Heart Bloodstone_, you can feel the gentle rhythm of a beating heart within the jar.

**Activate—Raise Jar** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))    **Effect** You hold the jar aloft, and a nimbus of crimson energy surrounds your body. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to AC until the start of your next turn.

**Activate—Proclaim Resilence** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;  **Requirements** You worship [Arazni](/Deities.aspx?ID=326) or are favored by her; **Effect** You make a loud and clear proclamation of your resilience (such as “I will not fall to the hands of my enemies!”). You gain [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2312) to void damage equal to your level until the beginning of your next turn.

**Destruction** The _Heart Bloodstone_ turns to dust if a worshipper of Arazni is slain while holding the _Bloodstone_ and cursing her name. Any breathing creature within 10 feet of the jar inhales the choking dust, taking 4d6 [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510) damage (DC 28 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Fortitude save). On a failure, the creature also takes 4 [persistent void damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86) (8 persistent void damage on a critical failure).

May contain spoilers from Dead God's Hand **Source** [The Dead God's Hand](/Sources.aspx?ID=370) pg. 144 **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** 3 --- **_Nethys Note: This artifact contains spoilers for The Dead God's Hand. Read at your own risk._** This fist-sized ruby would be close to priceless even if it weren't a magical artifact. So large and heavy for a ruby that most merchants would take it for a fake anyway, the _Heart of Sarnax_ pulses like a heartbeat whenever the wielder speaks aloud the name “Sarnax.” **Activate—Two Hearts as One** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You hold forth the _Heart of Sarnax_, targeting a living creature within 60 feet, then give the huge ruby a firm squeeze. The _Heart of Sarnax_ begins pounding in your grip, like a heart racing in panic or exertion, and the targeted creature feels their own heart speed up to match. Choose one of the following effects to apply to the targeted creature. **Bestow Vim** The target creature becomes [quickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=89), and it can use the extra action to [Stride](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305), [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306), or attempt an [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) check that resolves as a single action. Any Strikes made during this action are not affected by the creature's current multiple attack penalty, and any Athletics checks made during this action gain a +2 item bonus. If the creature uses the action to Stride, it gains a +10-foot item bonus to its Speed. This effect lasts for 1 minute, after which the target creature becomes [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=73) for 1 hour. **Crush Heart** ([death](/Traits.aspx?ID=571)) The target creature feels its heart pounding harder, and then suddenly feels it stop as its life essence is crushed. The creature takes 7d6 spirit damage and must attempt a DC 20 Fortitude save. A creature reduced to 0 HP by this damage is slain. **Critical Success** The creature takes no damage, but is [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) until the end of its next turn.
**Success** The creature takes half damage and is off-guard until the end of its next turn.
**Failure** The creature takes full damage, is off-guard until the end of its next turn, and is [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) 1 for 1 minute.
**Critical Failure** The creature takes double damage and is [stunned](/Conditions.aspx?ID=93) 3. When it recovers from being stunned, it is slowed 2 for 1 minute. **Destruction** By transforming the _Heart of Sarnax_ into a ruby version of Sarnax and then destroying the construct, the _Heart of Sarnax_ shatters into valuable but non-magical fragments.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 15"
    pfs="Restricted"
>
[Heartblood Ring](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2371)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 187

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn ring

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Sealed inside the hidden compartment of a gold ring, heartblood has an unmistakable coppery taste, along with a thick mouth feel. A whiff of the concoction is pleasantly stimulating.

---

**Stage 1 (1 Week)** The first time you enter this stage from a particular dose of _heartblood_, you are affected as if by [_regenerate_](/Spells.aspx?ID=248). Each round this effect functions, it attempts to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) one [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=46) or [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126) affecting you with a bonus equal to your class DC – 10. _Heartblood_ also reduces physical signs of aging, altering your appearance to that of vigorous adulthood for your ancestry. (Non-adults who drink _heartblood_ change only in apparent vigor, not age.)

 You have [fast healing](/Rules.aspx?ID=796) equal to half your level, as well as resistance to negative damage and poison damage equal to half your level. Also, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to saving throws (or any other defense) against [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=40) effects, disease, [paralysis](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28), poison, and [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=145). Treat the outcome of any saving throw you roll against death, paralyze, or sleep effects as one step better.

---

**Stage 2 (1 Month)** You gain [low-light vision](/Rules.aspx?ID=416), or you gain [darkvision](/Rules.aspx?ID=415) if your ancestry already has low-light vision. Reduce your current and maximum Hit Points by 2 × your level; you are [doomed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=9). You develop a pallor and a dislike of [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=407), especially sunlight. If suddenly exposed to bright light, you are [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=7) until the end of your next turn. While in an area of sunlight, you remain dazzled until 1 round after the exposure ends. Normal food is unsatisfying, and you have urges to consume blood; when confronted with the opportunity to do so, you must succeed at a Will save to avoid it. Doing so once after each time you roll initiative is enough. Your normal coloration returns for a few hours after you drink blood.

 If you die at this stage or higher, your body becomes a bloody mist that sinks 6 feet into the ground. The third night thereafter, you rise from the earth as a [vampire](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=97) with the alignment of the _heartblood's_ creator. You are under the control of the _heartblood's_ creator unless your level is higher than that creature's. The controlling vampire senses you and guides you to them via psychic link. Significant destruction of your body and circumstances that prevent the formation of [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) stop this effect.

---

**Stage 3 (1 Month)** You gain darkvision and now have fast healing equal to your level. A death effect can't automatically kill you or increase your dying value. Reduce your current and maximum Hit Points by 4 × your level, rounded up, instead of 2 × your level; you are doomed 2. Your hunger for blood increases, so if you fail to drink a cup or so each day, you are considered to have gone without food that day. You are also [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35) while in sunlight, becoming slowed 2 after 1 minute. Your shadow is wispy, and your reflection in mirrors ghostly, which are apparent signs of vampirism to those who know such facts.

---

**Stage 4** You die.

---

**Purging** _Heartblood_ loses its potency if the vampire who created it is destroyed. However, a dose of _heartblood_ imposes a –2 status penalty to your saving throws against the powers of the vampire who created it.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<column gap="tiny">
